summary_for_children: Al-Hashr means The Gathering. It speaks of generosity among believers, and ends with the beautiful names of Allah and the image of a mountain humbled by the Quran.
environment_concept: A great mountain, humbled (59:21), and a reading stand with the ayahs of Allah's names (59:22-24; the names are read from the verified text, not drawn in the sky).
architecture_and_scenery: A towering mountain with cracks of light, a valley of palm trees, and a calm sky where the names appear as calligraphic text only.

areas.description: The names written as text in the sky.

primary_mechanic.text: Run a community aid centre where those who give prefer others even when in need (59:9).

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Community and Its Responsibilities
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Hashr recalls a difficult historical event involving the exile of a community and teaches about the distribution of resources, generosity, and responsibility. It praises those who care for others, even when they themselves have needs.

world_idea.title: The House of Generosity
world_idea.description: Organize a community aid center, learn about sharing resources justly, and discover how a community can care for people in need.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
